steps.title: Etna
steps.body: Nerello Mascalese grows mainly on the slopes of Mount Etna, Europe's highest active volcano, at 400 to over 1,000 m. Most vineyards are on the north side, around villages like Passopisciaro, Randazzo and Solicchiata. Smaller amounts grow elsewhere in north-east Sicily, like Faro near Messina.

steps.title: Altitude
steps.body: Altitude cools Etna's vineyards: nights can be 15 to 20 degrees cooler than days, keeping acidity and aroma. Etna receives more rain than the rest of Sicily, and harvest can run into late October. It's one of the few places in southern Italy with an almost Alpine climate.

steps.prompt: Match each term to Nerello Mascalese.
steps.explanation: Nerello Mascalese belongs to north-east Sicily.

steps.title: Partners
steps.body: Etna Rosso DOC must be at least 80% Nerello Mascalese. The rest can be Nerello Cappuccio, which adds colour and softness. Old Etna vineyards are often field blends, with white grapes mixed in. Carricante is Etna's main white grape.

steps.explanation: Nerello Cappuccio can make up the rest.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Nerello Mascalese grows mainly on Etna's north slope
Altitude gives cool nights and late harvests
Etna Rosso is at least 80% Nerello Mascalese
